study_type.claude: Survey (descriptive quantitative + Grounded Theory coding of open answers)
study_type.nlm: Survey (mixed quantitative descriptive and qualitative GT coding)

research_method.claude: Online personal-opinion survey (Molléri et al. guidelines), pilot-validated; descriptive statistics plus Grounded Theory open and axial coding; 7 RQs; 58 valid of 61 responses
research_method.nlm: Survey with quantitative descriptive statistics and qualitative Grounded Theory coding; guidelines of Molléri et al.; pilot and expert review; 7 RQs
research_method.value: Online personal-opinion survey (Molléri et al. guidelines, pilot-tested) on human and organizational productivity factors selected from the literature; descriptive statistics for closed items and Grounded Theory open and axial coding (phases 1-2) of open answers; 7 RQs; 58 valid responses of 61

context.claude: Industry; Brazilian software companies during COVID-19 remote work; 58 team members from all regions (mostly Northeast and Southeast), 91.4% in teams of 0-20
context.nlm: Industry; Brazilian software development companies across all regions; 58 team members; 91.4% in teams of 0-20
context.value: industry; development teams of Brazilian software companies in pandemic remote work; 58 team members (developers, managers, testers, designers, analysts) from all Brazilian regions, mostly Northeast and Southeast, 91.4% in teams of up to 20 people

remote_covid.note: Forced remote work during COVID-19 is the study's subject.

cat_productivity.note: Only perceived productivity (Q28 self-rating, Q29 open answers), which goes to Survey.

cat_collaboration.note: Team collaboration (Q14), ease of communication (Q17), communication tools (Q18-Q20).

cat_satisfaction.note: Motivation (Q21), feelings during isolation (Q22), health practices (Q23).

cat_activity.note: NotebookLM labels perceived turnover 'Activity', but it is not repository activity.

cat_delivery.note: NotebookLM labels task time distribution (Q12) 'Delivery/Process', but it is a perceived rating, not a delivery metric.

cat_agile.note: Borderline: only the perceived rating of time distribution for tasks (Q12, and Claude adds work-routine Q13), labelled Process by both; no sprint or ceremony metric.

cat_survey.note: All measures are self-reported survey items (ordinal and 1-8 scales, open questions).

evidence.quote: For this, we design and conduct a personal opinion survey through an online questionnaire to collect the software team members' perceptions on this topic. We based the survey's design on the guidelines established by Mólleri et al. [17, 18].
used only the GT's phases 1 and 2 to identify the categories and their relationships
The population selected for the study were people who worked in development teams of Brazilian software companies.
Our survey was made available from 12 to 31 May 2020, in several lists and groups of IT professionals in Brazil. There were 61 participants, 3 of them did not meet the validation criteria
This global crisis has affected the software industry, as companies have adopted work from home (remote work) in order to protect their employees [9].
93.1% consider they have a collaborative team and 84.5% have easy communication with their co-workers; 84.5% feel motivated;
How motivated do you feel to perform your tasks? (not very motivated 1 - 8 very motivated) Check the options that show your feelings during the period of social isolation.
In question Q12, we analyzed the time distribution to perform tasks by asking participants to rate this factor using the following scale (unsatisfactory, regular, good, excellent).
we identified that 74.1% of the participants consider their productivity remains good or excellent
